google/gemini-2.5-flash.mistake: The natural language statement 'For Brayan, finding happiness and pursuing perfection are mutually exclusive' implies that Brayan cannot both find happiness AND pursue perfection (i.e., ¬(p_8(Brayan) ∧ p_9(Brayan))). However, the First-Order Logic (FOL) statement p_8(Brayan) ⊕ p_9(Brayan) represents an exclusive OR (XOR). XOR means that exactly one of the two propositions is true. While XOR *does* imply they are mutually exclusive (they cannot both be true), it also implies that at least one of them *must* be true. The natural language statement does not necessitate that one of them must be true; it only states that they cannot *both* be true.
